title: A constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates yields a logarithmic spiral

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates yields a logarithmic spiral

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a tubular structure whose growth is unequal on its two sides, a constant ratio between the rates of growth in the longitudinal and transverse directions generally produces a logarithmic spiral, the value of the ratio fixing the spiral's constant angle, with the circle and the straight line as limiting cases.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}, the ratio fixing \alpha; \alpha = 90^\circ circle, \alpha \to 0 straight line

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In other words, in such a structure as we have presupposed, the existence or maintenance of a constant ratio between the rates of extension or growth in the vertical and transverse directions will lead, in general, to the development of a logarithmic spiral; the magnitude of that ratio will determine the character (that is to say, the constant angle) of the spiral;

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Forces producing a spiral”. Scope: tubular shells and horns growing by unequal accretion

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}, the ratio fixing \alpha; \alpha = 90^\circ circle, \alpha \to 0 straight line

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.79

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim supplies a quantitative relation between measurable ratios and spiral angle. Existing accretionary hard parts retain growth histories, allowing standard geometric tests across representative shells and horns.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate local longitudinal and transverse accretion rates from successive growth increments and test whether their ratio is constant and predicts a constant-angle logarithmic centerline. Variable ratios should predict systematic departures from logarithmic form.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Static growth lines are proxies for rates.

Tube cross-section and torsion can complicate the ideal model.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Constancy of the growth-rate ratio, and its match to the spiral angle, can be read from increments on existing shells. Public scans and photographs cover common molluscs well enough to accept or reject the relation, with horns as a thinner additional scope. The measurement is standard geometric morphometrics and does not need new collections.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Along growth lines of tubular shells and horns, measure the ratio of longitudinal to transverse extension and the spiral angle. A ratio that stays constant and matches the angle supports the claim; a drifting ratio that still yields a logarithmic spiral, or a constant ratio that does not, refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Horns are less often scanned with usable growth lines than mollusc shells.

Within an ideal logarithmic model the ratio and the angle are linked by definition, so the empirical test is constancy on real specimens.

fields.label: Dimension scores

discriminating power: 0.65
